i0-context.title: Load baseline context
i0-context.imperative: Load the handed-in goal and context (what you are resolving) and the starting questions, if any. Read the glossary and the topic's relevant code/docs. Record pass when loaded.
i0-context.finding: Loaded Charter goal, user intent, inherited doctrine, README, source layout, tests, and Charter starting questions.

q1.title: What is the project-specific meaning of proven effectiveness?
q1.imperative: Decision: define what constitutes proof that a skill change is effective. Ask the human one scenario-tested question; append follow-ups for material doctrine axes.
q1.finding: Decision, human answer: Verify all mechanistic pieces cleanly. Treat feedback collected from agents in real projects as the effectiveness input; do not invent arbitrary projects or synthetic proof cases.

zc-consolidate.title: Consolidate behind the finish gate
zc-consolidate.imperative: Do NOT record this until joint understanding is reached. Write the interrogation record from templates/INTERROGATION_RECORD.template.json (each question typed fact|decision; each resolved decision carrying its human_answer; each resolved fact its code_evidence) and capture the counterpart's explicit sign-off. Run `py scripts/verify_interrogation.py <record>` — it MUST exit 0 (it refuses consolidation without the joint-understanding sign-off, and refuses any self-answered decision). Record pass only after exit 0, then `consolidate`.
zc-consolidate.finding: Signed record passed scripts/verify_interrogation.py: all decisions have human answers, no questions remain open, and the project owner confirmed the shared understanding.

q2.title: How should collected feedback govern a skill change?
q2.imperative: Decision: determine whether real-project feedback is advisory, a required input for changes, or a release/review blocker. Ask one concrete scenario-tested question with a recommendation.
q2.finding: Decision, human answer: Real-project feedback is advisory, not a hard evidence or review gate. It should nevertheless be aggressively pursued; the project may need to improve how that pursuit is operationalized.

q3.title: What disposition does each advisory feedback item require?
q3.imperative: Decision: set a concrete disposition rule for collected feedback: investigate and act, defer with reason and revisit trigger, or reject with reason. Ask one scenario-tested question with a recommendation.
q3.finding: Decision, human answer: Do not impose per-item disposition. Collect lightweight freeform post-job feedback (“how did it go?”); improve it, if needed, by inviting positives and negatives. A later issue interprets feedback and chooses implementation.

q4.title: May feedback collection block completion?
q4.imperative: Decision: establish whether a job may finish when feedback is absent, empty, or merely brief. Ask one scenario-tested question with a recommendation.
q4.finding: Decision, human answer: No. Feedback collection must not block task completion when absent, empty, or brief.

q5.title: What repository actions may agents take directly?
q5.imperative: Decision: establish agent authority for local commits, pushes, pull requests, and merging to main. Ask one scenario-tested question with a recommendation.
q5.finding: Decision, human answer: Agents may make local commits. Pushes, PR creation, and merges to main require explicit human approval, although approval may be granted in advance for specified work.

q6.title: What verification is required for a changed mechanism?
q6.imperative: Decision: define the test and validation threshold for a behavior or workflow-mechanism change in this skill corpus. Ask one scenario-tested question with a recommendation.
q6.finding: Decision, human answer: Yes. Workflow-mechanism changes require targeted automated tests plus the relevant broader suite, except where an explicit no-test-surface rationale applies.

q7.title: Are any other project-specific doctrine departures needed?
q7.imperative: Decision: seek explicit confirmation that remaining engineering-rubric axes retain the inherited rigorous default, unless the human identifies a named subsystem departure. Ask concisely.
q7.finding: Decision, human answer: Yes. All remaining engineering-rubric areas retain the inherited rigorous default; no further project-specific departures are identified.

consolidation.summary: Project-specific doctrine resolved and human-confirmed; compile lightweight feedback, verification, and Git authority deltas.
